description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, while adding the flow-rate inlet BC (op-2qsf). NOT fixed.

SYMPTOM. In step()'s pressure corrector, the mass-flux correction phi -= rho_f*rAU_f*snGrad(p)*|Sf| is applied to INTERNAL faces only; boundary faces keep the predictor value phi_HbyA. A prescribed-velocity (or prescribed-mass-flow) inlet is unaffected -- its boundary flux is written back explicitly from the BC -- but a fixed-pressure outlet's boundary flux is the uncorrected predictor.

MEASUREMENT. 1.0 g/s prescribed at the inlet (exact by construction), 200 W uniformly distributed, run to steady state, outlet flux read from phi's outlet patch:
  n =  8 cells: m_out = 9.929649e-4 kg/s, -0.7035 % against the inlet
  n = 16 cells: m_out = 9.968502e-4 kg/s, -0.3150 %
  n = 32 cells: m_out = 9.985182e-4 kg/s, -0.1482 %
Halving with each refinement => FIRST-ORDER TRUNCATION, not a conservation bug. Chief cause is the zero-gradient extrapolation of the outlet face velocity from the last cell centre while the flow is still accelerating through that half cell. The steady ENERGY balance closes far tighter over the same runs (200.0574 / 200.0002 / 200.0000 W against a 200 W source).

TRIED AND REJECTED. Recomputing the non-fixed-velocity boundary fluxes from the corrected U after the pressure correction moves n = 8 from -0.7035 % to -0.5364 % only -- it is not the dominant term, and it perturbs every existing test's numbers for a fraction of the error. Not worth taking on those terms without a proper look at the outlet face-value reconstruction.

Documented in the accuracy caveat on OPCPFluidArray::get_outlet_mass_flowrate_actual and in the doc comment of lateral_coupling::tests::mass_flow_inlet_closes_the_steady_energy_balance.
title: OPCPFluidArray: boundary face flux phi is never pressure-corrected -- first-order outlet mass-balance deficit

description: ~20 lines, two places, in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine. full_simulation/mod.rs:1985-1988 computes (timestep_ms - calc_ms).round().abs() -- the .abs() turns an OVERRUN into a positive sleep budget, so a 150 ms step against a 100 ms timestep sleeps 49 ms AFTER already overrunning. :1990 computes from_millis(x - 1) BEFORE the > 1 guard at :1992, underflowing u64 at 0 (latent under the mandatory release profile; panics in debug).
